title: hotset-aware block arena + block coalescing to reduce KV cache fragmentation and contention
author: Aditi Rao
description: Motivation: production workloads showed persistent tail latency spikes and increased memory fragmentation when the paged KV cache experienced high churn from mixed-length sessions. This PR introduces a hotset-aware block arena and an opportunistic block coalescing pass to reduce fragmentation, lower lock contention, and improve tail latency without changing the public pin/release API. In practice the arena allocates fixed-size blocks organized into lightweight per-GPU arenas (cohorts) to avoid a global allocator lock under high concurrency. Each block carries a compact lifespan hint derived from sequence-length histograms and recent access telemetry; the eviction path uses these hints to form an eviction skyline that prioritizes reclaiming cold fragments while preserving the hot prefix. The coalescing pass runs opportunistically during low-util windows or when a cohort's fragmentation ratio crosses a threshold, merging adjacent free blocks to form larger contiguous segments and enabling larger KV slices to avoid scatter I/O. The change is backwards compatible: it reuses existing block headers and the pinning API; only a new 'slice_class' runtime metric is exposed. Implementation notes: new arena.rs encapsulates per-device arenas and lock sharding, block_allocator.rs moves to arena-backed allocations, eviction.rs gets hotset heuristics and the skyline logic, metrics.rs adds fragmentation_ratio and coalesce_runs counters, and the scheduler's batching path uses cohort-aware affinity to reduce cross-GPU cache traffic. Testing and safety: added deterministic unit tests for coalescing, a stress test that simulates mixed short/long requests, and a perf-canary harness that compares throughput/latency with/without the arena. Rollout plan: feature-flagged behind runtime_config.block_arena.enabled, staged rollout to dedicated clusters, monitor fragmentation_ratio and p99_latency dashboards, canary to 1% traffic for 24h then 10%/50%/100% if no regressions. Benchmarks: on benchmark-lab with an 8xA100 cluster and mixed 32/2048 token workloads we see median latency -6% p50, tail latency p99 -18%, and end-to-end token throughput +12% at target SLO; memory overhead for metadata is ~1.8% per-GPU. The PR also documents operational knobs for tuning coalescing thresholds and per-cohort max_free_run before compaction. See release notes and runbook for rollback steps.

review_comments: Miguel Santos: Can you explain why we prefer opportunistic coalescing versus eager coalescing? I worry about CPU impact during peak load.

Aditi Rao: Opportunistic coalescing is intentionally low-priority and gated by fragmentation_ratio and a per-cohort grace timer; CPU impact was measured in the perf-canary and stayed below 3% of runtime on our 8xA100 setup.

release_notes: Introduce hotset-aware per-GPU block arena and opportunistic block coalescing to reduce KV cache fragmentation and tail latency. Default disabled; rollout gated by runtime_config.block_arena.enabled. Improvements: p50 -6%, p99 -18%, throughput +12% in mixed workloads. Operational metrics: fragmentation_ratio, coalesce_runs, slice_class distribution.
